response: The use of complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) therapies by U.S. adults with chronic disease-related functional limitations has indeed changed from 2002 to 2007. According to the data, there was a significant overall increase in CAM use among this population during this time period, particularly among those with changing and maintaining body position limitations. This suggests that individuals with chronic disease-related functional limitations are turning to CAM therapies as a way to manage their conditions and improve their quality of life.
